q:
בת 94, גרה לבדה עד האשפוז, לא ידוע על ירידה קוגניטיבית. מאושפזת במחלקה פנימית בשל אלח דם (SEPSIS) ממקור של דלקת בדרכי השתן. היא נושאת קתטר שתן ומטופלת באנטיביוטיקה דרך הוריד. רופא גריאטר נקרא לתת יעוץ בשל מצב של אי-שקט ובלבול. בבדיקה נראית כאובה, סובלת מאי שקט פסיכו-מוטורי בולט, ליקוי בקשב, חוסר התמצאות במקום ובזמן. רשימת תרופות שמקבלת:   
 ROCEPHIN  
 ENOXAPARIN (CLEXAN)  
 PARACETAMOL  
 OXAZEPAM (VABEN)  
 RAMIPRIL (TRITACE)  
 TROSPIUM (SPASMEX)  
 BROTIZOLAM (BONDORMIN)  
 מה צריך לייעץ בהתייחס לטיפול התרופתי שהמטופלת מקבלת?
o: להפסיק טיפול ב- VABEN שקיבלה בביתה
להפסיק את הטיפול ב- TROSPIUM (SPSMEX)
להחליף את ה-BROTIZOLAM (BONDORMIN) ב- ZOLPIDEM (ZODORM)
להוסיף טיפול קבוע ב- TRAMADOL לאיזון כאב
explanation:
The patient has a **delirium** presentation in the setting of sepsis and urinary infection: psychomotor agitation, impaired attention and disorientation. Older adults are vulnerable to anticholinergic adverse effects. Trospium is an anticholinergic bladder drug; its indication should be reviewed when reducing medication burden. A urinary catheter alone does not establish that it no longer has an indication (Hazzard 8e, pp. 888–889; Beers 2023, pp. 2066, 2074).

**A. Stop the oxazepam taken at home.** Wrong, prolonged benzodiazepine use may produce physical dependence. Inference: given that dependence and withdrawal can cause delirium, dose reduction should be planned according to the use history rather than automatically stopping abruptly (Beers, p. 2060; Hazzard, p. 889).
**B. Stop trospium.** Correct, this is the official answer. Trospium is listed among drugs with strong anticholinergic properties, a group that may worsen delirium (Beers, pp. 2066, 2074).
**C. Replace brotizolam with zolpidem.** Wrong, switching does not remove the delirium risk: Z-drugs are also associated with delirium (Beers, p. 2060).
**D. Add regular tramadol for pain.** Wrong, adding an opioid requires pain assessment and consideration of delirium risk, rather than automatic scheduled treatment (Beers, p. 2066).

Tramadol is an opioid that also inhibits serotonin reuptake. It can have central adverse effects and is not an automatic solution for pain during delirium; its mechanism should not be described as anticholinergic (Hazzard, p. 1061, Table 68-6).

Delirium management begins with nonpharmacologic approaches and includes reducing exposure to aggravating medications according to their indications (Hazzard, p. 888; Beers, p. 2066).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2060, 2066, 2074; Hazzard 8e, pp. 888–889, 1061.

q: מטופל בן 72 עם דמנציה קלה-בינונית מגיע לחדר מיון עם חשד לאוטם שריר הלב. הוא מסרב לטיפול ואומר 'אני רוצה לחזור הביתה'. איך יש לנהוג?
o: לכבד את סירובו ולשחרר אותו מיד
להתחיל טיפול בכוח כי מדובר במצב מסכן חיים
לבחון את יכולתו לקבל החלטות מדעת ולפעול בהתאם
לבקש מבן המשפחה להחליט במקומו
explanation:
**הסכמה מדעת** דורשת הבנה ובחירה מרצון ביחס לטיפול המוצע. לכן, כהסקה מדרישות החוק, יש לברר מה המטופל מבין ומה משמעות סירובו לפני החלטה על שחרור או טיפול בניגוד לרצונו. החוק מסדיר בנפרד מצבי סכנה וחירום; חשד לאוטם אינו מבטל מעצמו את הצורך לבדוק את תנאיהם (סעיפים 13 ו־15, עמ׳ PDF 8 ו־15).
"לא יינתן טיפול רפואי למטופל אלא אם כן נתן לכך המטופל הסכמה מדעת לפי הוראות פרק זה." (עמ׳ 8).

**א. לכבד את סירובו ולשחרר אותו מיד.** שגויה, שחרור מיידי מדלג על הבירור אם הסירוב מבוסס על הבנת המצב והטיפול. זו הסקה מחובת מסירת מידע המאפשר החלטה מרצון (סעיף 13, עמ׳ PDF 8).
**ב. להתחיל טיפול בכוח כי מדובר במצב מסכן חיים.** שגויה, החוק אינו מתיר כפייה אוטומטית בכל סכנה: התנגדות בסכנה חמורה כפופה למסלול ועדת אתיקה ולתנאים, ובחירום נבחנת האפשרות לקבל הסכמה מדעת (סעיף 15, עמ׳ PDF 15).
**ג. לבחון את יכולתו לקבל החלטות מדעת ולפעול בהתאם.** נכונה, בדיקת ההבנה והבחירה מאפשרת להחליט אם מדובר בסירוב מדעת או במצב המחייב מסלול אחר לפי החוק; זו הסקה מדרישות סעיפים 13 ו־15 (עמ׳ PDF 8 ו־15).
**ד. לבקש מבן המשפחה להחליט במקומו.** שגויה, עצם הקרבה המשפחתית אינה המינוי המתואר בחוק. יש לברר סמכות ייצוג כדין במקום להחליף את החלטת המטופל אוטומטית בהחלטת קרוב (סעיף 16, עמ׳ PDF 16).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה; עמודי PDF, עמ׳ 8, 15, 16.
ref: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו-1996 · PDF pp. 8–9, 15–16; sections 13, 14(a), 15
label: Source: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו-1996 · PDF pp. 8–9, 15–16; sections 13, 14(a), 15

q: A patient has a stage 4 pressure injury over the sacrum. Which description matches this stage?
o: Full-thickness loss with exposed deep structures and osteomyelitis risk
Intact skin with nonblanchable erythema and preserved deeper tissue
Partial-thickness loss with a moist wound bed and a serum-filled blister
Visible subcutaneous fat with granulation and covered bone and tendon
explanation:
A **stage 4 pressure injury** exposes deep structures such as bone, muscle, or tendon. Hazzard describes osteomyelitis as a common outcome when bone is exposed; this distinguishes it from the shallower tissue involvement in earlier stages (pp. 686–687).
"Full-thickness loss of skin with exposure of bone, muscle, tendon, ligament, or cartilage." (p. 686).
"Osteomyelitis is a common outcome when there is exposure of bone and should be considered the cause of nonhealing in any stage 4 PI." (p. 686).

**A. Full-thickness loss with exposed deep structures and osteomyelitis risk.** Correct, this captures the deep exposure of stage 4 and the source-described risk when bone is exposed (p. 686).
**B. Intact skin with nonblanchable erythema and preserved deeper tissue.** Wrong, intact skin with nonblanchable erythema describes stage 1, not the full-thickness deep exposure of stage 4 (pp. 686–687).
**C. Partial-thickness loss with a moist wound bed and a serum-filled blister.** Wrong, partial-thickness loss and a serum-filled blister describe stage 2 rather than exposed deep structures (pp. 686–687).
**D. Visible subcutaneous fat with granulation and covered bone and tendon.** Wrong, stage 3 can expose fat, but the source explicitly excludes exposed muscle, tendon, or bone from that stage (pp. 686–687).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 686, 687.

q: In the study of patients with Parkinson disease or dementia described in Hazzard, honey-thick liquids were compared with nectar-thick liquids and chin-down posture. Which result distinguishes short-term aspiration from pneumonia during follow-up?
o: Less short-term aspiration and a lower follow-up pneumonia rate
More short-term aspiration and a lower follow-up pneumonia rate
Less short-term aspiration and a similar follow-up pneumonia rate
More short-term aspiration and a similar follow-up pneumonia rate
explanation:
**Aspiration during testing** and **subsequent pneumonia** were different outcomes. Hazzard states: "In the short term, aspiration is reduced with honey-thick liquids as compared with both nectar-thick and chin-down posture interventions" (p. 450). The strategies were equally effective for pneumonia prevention over three months (p. 450).

**A. Less short-term aspiration and a lower follow-up pneumonia rate.** Wrong, the aspiration finding fits, but the source does not report superior pneumonia prevention with honey-thick liquids (p. 450).
**B. More short-term aspiration and a lower follow-up pneumonia rate.** Wrong, this contradicts both the lower short-term aspiration and the similar pneumonia-prevention results (p. 450).
**C. Less short-term aspiration and a similar follow-up pneumonia rate.** Correct, this preserves the distinction between reduced short-term aspiration and similar pneumonia prevention during follow-up (p. 450).
**D. More short-term aspiration and a similar follow-up pneumonia rate.** Wrong, similar pneumonia prevention fits, but the source reports less, not more, short-term aspiration with honey-thick liquids (p. 450).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 450.

q: A 77-year-old woman lives independently, manages her medications, and drives. Despite trazodone 50 mg nightly for three months, she reports fragmented sleep. MMSE is 28/30. Her diary records going to bed at 8 pm, falling asleep at 11 pm, repeated awakenings, and final waking at 4 am. She spends most days indoors watching television. Which behavioral approach is consistent with the source's sleep recommendations?
o: Advance bedtime further and remain in bed through prolonged wakefulness
Schedule prolonged daytime naps and vary the morning rising time
Increase moderate daytime activity and follow a consistent waking schedule
Schedule strenuous exercise just before bedtime and watch television in bed
explanation:
**Behavioral sleep care** includes activity and a regular sleep-wake routine (pp. 661-662). Hazzard states: "A moderate exercise program can improve sleep in healthy sedentary older adults" (p. 662), while stimulus control advises getting up at the same time and going to bed when sleepy. These are supported behavioral approaches; the vignette does not establish a single root cause.

**A. Advance bedtime further and remain in bed through prolonged wakefulness.** Wrong, stimulus control advises going to bed when sleepy and leaving bed during prolonged inability to sleep, not extending wakefulness in bed (p. 662).
**B. Schedule prolonged daytime naps and vary the morning rising time.** Wrong, the source advises avoiding naps or limiting them and keeping a regular schedule (pp. 661-662).
**C. Increase moderate daytime activity and follow a consistent waking schedule.** Correct, this combines moderate activity with a consistent schedule; applying it here is an inference from the sedentary routine and sleep history (pp. 661-662).
**D. Schedule strenuous exercise just before bedtime and watch television in bed.** Wrong, the source discourages strenuous exercise close to bedtime and limits in-bed activities to sleep or sex (p. 662).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 661, 662.

q: An 82-year-old man with vascular dementia is hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure. He is usually oriented to person but now fails to recognize his daughter, has difficulty sustaining attention, and was awake overnight trying to catch a bus. Which interpretation best fits the acute mental-status change?
o: Progression of dementia accounting for the overnight fluctuation
Delirium superimposed on dementia during acute illness
Stable baseline dementia accounting for the new inattention
Expected normal aging accounting for the abrupt confusion
explanation:
**Acute onset and inattention** are central features of delirium. Dementia increases vulnerability, and acute illness and sleep deprivation can contribute; identifying delirium does not establish a single cause, because its etiology is usually multifactorial (pp. 881, 883).
"Acute onset and inattention are the central features of delirium." (p. 883).
"With delirium, the mental status changes typically occur over hours to days, in contrast to the changes that occur with dementia" (p. 883).

**A. Progression of dementia accounting for the overnight fluctuation.** Wrong, dementia generally develops insidiously, whereas this new change occurred overnight (p. 883).
**B. Delirium superimposed on dementia during acute illness.** Correct, the abrupt change, inattention and sleep-wake disturbance fit delirium occurring in a patient already vulnerable because of dementia (pp. 881, 883).
**C. Stable baseline dementia accounting for the new inattention.** Wrong, a new attentional deficit and change from the usual state require recognition of an acute syndrome, rather than attribution to an unchanged baseline (p. 883).
**D. Expected normal aging accounting for the abrupt confusion.** Wrong, acute confusion with inattention is a defining clinical pattern of delirium, not a description of stable aging (p. 883).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 881, 883.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp. 881, 883–885

q: A 77-year-old man with early Parkinson disease lives alone and independently manages his IADLs. His daughter requests power of attorney because she believes he has dementia. He has mild rest tremor, cogwheeling, and bradykinesia. MoCA is 24/30 with visuospatial and executive errors, but he accurately describes his medicines, manages finances online, and drives safely. Which response addresses the discrepancy between cognitive screening and function?
o: Arrange formal neuropsychological assessment of the cognitive findings
Treat the MoCA result as establishing loss of decision-making capacity
Diagnose Parkinson disease dementia from the screening result
Treat his independent function as excluding cognitive impairment
explanation:
**Cognitive impairment in Parkinson disease** does not necessarily meet the definition of dementia. Parkinson disease dementia requires impairment severe enough to interfere with daily activities, and screening findings should be interpreted with baseline function; formal testing can characterize the discrepancy (pp. 869–870, 906). The diagnostic criteria include "cognitive impairment severe enough to impair activities of daily living" (p. 870).

**A. Arrange formal neuropsychological assessment of the cognitive findings.** Correct, formal assessment can characterize subtle deficits and relate them to baseline functioning before a dementia diagnosis is made (pp. 869, 906).
**B. Treat the MoCA result as establishing loss of decision-making capacity.** Wrong, a screening result does not determine decision-making capacity; the source states that no single cutoff score can do so (p. 153).
**C. Diagnose Parkinson disease dementia from the screening result.** Wrong, the stem does not establish cognitive interference with daily independence, a required feature of Parkinson disease dementia (p. 870).
**D. Treat his independent function as excluding cognitive impairment.** Wrong, Parkinson disease mild cognitive impairment can occur without impairment sufficient to interfere with functional independence (p. 870).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 153, 869, 870, 906.
ref: Hazzard Ch 57 — COGNITIVE CHANGES IN NORMAL AND PATHOLOGIC AGING
chapterTitle: Cognitive Changes in Normal and Pathologic Aging

q: A 74-year-old woman with depression and osteoarthritis has persistent hip pain despite acetaminophen. She takes sertraline and declines NSAIDs because of gastrointestinal concerns. The team is considering a supervised change to duloxetine. Which source-described action explains its potential analgesic role?
o: Inhibition of cyclooxygenase to reduce prostaglandin formation
Modulation of pain pathways through serotonin and norepinephrine
Blockade of voltage-gated calcium channels to reduce excitability
Increased GABA activity to reduce neuronal excitability
explanation:
**Duloxetine**, an SNRI, can be used as a coanalgesic because serotonin and norepinephrine modulate pain pathways. Hazzard describes inhibition of ascending pain pathways and promotion of descending inhibitory pathways; this explains an analgesic role without establishing that it is the safest option for this individual (pp. 1063-1064).
"Modulation of pain pathway via serotonin, norepinephrine" (p. 1063).
"By increasing the activity of serotonin and norepinephrine, these medications modulate the pain pathway to inhibit ascending pain pathways and promote descending pain inhibitory pathways." (p. 1064).

**A. Inhibition of cyclooxygenase to reduce prostaglandin formation.** Wrong, the source assigns cyclooxygenase inhibition to NSAIDs, not to duloxetine (p. 1063).
**B. Modulation of pain pathways through serotonin and norepinephrine.** Correct, this is the SNRI mechanism listed for duloxetine and explained in the text (pp. 1063-1064).
**C. Blockade of voltage-gated calcium channels to reduce excitability.** Wrong, voltage-gated calcium-channel blockade is the mechanism listed for gabapentinoids (p. 1063).
**D. Increased GABA activity to reduce neuronal excitability.** Wrong, increased GABA activity is the mechanism listed for benzodiazepines, not SNRIs (p. 1064).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1063, 1064.

q: A patient with HFpEF receives diuretics for congestion. Excessive diuresis is followed by fatigue, lower blood pressure, and prerenal azotemia. Which hemodynamic change explains this volume sensitivity?
o: Increased ventricular filling volume with increased stroke volume
Increased ventricular filling volume with decreased stroke volume
Decreased ventricular filling volume with decreased stroke volume
Decreased ventricular filling volume with increased stroke volume
explanation:
**Volume sensitivity in HFpEF** means that excessive diuresis can reduce filling and subsequently reduce forward output. Hazzard links this change to fatigue, relative hypotension, and worsening prerenal azotemia (p. 1186). Overly zealous diuresis can cause "a reduction in left ventricular diastolic volume, with a resultant decline in stroke volume and cardiac output" (p. 1186).

**A. Increased ventricular filling volume with increased stroke volume.** Wrong, excessive diuresis lowers filling volume; the source describes a fall, not a rise, in stroke volume (p. 1186).
**B. Increased ventricular filling volume with decreased stroke volume.** Wrong, decreased stroke volume fits, but the accompanying filling-volume change is a reduction rather than an increase (p. 1186).
**C. Decreased ventricular filling volume with decreased stroke volume.** Correct, it matches the source sequence: reduced diastolic volume followed by reduced stroke volume and cardiac output (p. 1186).
**D. Decreased ventricular filling volume with increased stroke volume.** Wrong, reduced filling volume fits, but the source describes declining rather than increasing stroke volume in this setting (p. 1186).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1186.

q: בן 73, סובל בחודשים האחרונים מכאב נוירופתי המפריע לו בחיי היום יום. מתוך התרופות האפשרויות לטיפול איזה מעקב נדרש בעקבות תופעת לוואי מתאימה?
o: ELATROLET (Amitriptyline) מעקב קצב לב כי גורם לברדיקרדיה
TEGRETOL (Carbamazepine) מעקב אלקטרוליטים כי גורם להיפוקלמיה
CYMBALTA (Duloxetine) מעקב לחץ דם כי מעלה לחץ דם
LYRICA (Pregabalin) מעקב תפקודי כבד כי גורם לפגיעה כבדית
explanation:
Official answer: ג

**Duloxetine**, an SNRI, may raise blood pressure through its noradrenergic effects. Blood-pressure monitoring therefore correctly pairs the drug with an adverse effect and the relevant surveillance (pp. 1064, 1647).

**A. Amitriptyline: monitor heart rate because it causes bradycardia.** Wrong, the source describes tachycardia among anticholinergic adverse effects; bradycardia is not the effect used for this pairing (p. 1064).
**B. Carbamazepine: monitor electrolytes because it causes hypokalemia.** Wrong, monitoring is important because of hyponatremia, a fall in sodium, not the hypokalemia stated in the option (pp. 1063–1065).
**C. Duloxetine: monitor blood pressure because it can increase it.** Correct, the source describes possible blood-pressure elevation with SNRIs and recommends routine vital-sign monitoring (p. 1647).
**D. Pregabalin: monitor liver function because it causes hepatic injury.** Wrong, the source emphasizes low-dose initiation, tolerability and renal function with gabapentinoids; it does not provide hepatic injury as the basis for the proposed monitoring (pp. 1063–1065).

The additional source for blood-pressure monitoring during SNRI treatment is Hazzard 8e, p. 1647.

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1063, 1064, 1065, 1647.

q: In the epidural steroid injection RCT of 400 older adults with lumbar spinal stenosis, what did adding glucocorticoid to lidocaine achieve?
o: Proof that lidocaine alone has no effect compared with placebo
Minimal or no additional short-term disability or leg-pain benefit
Proof that steroid injections outperform a placebo injection
A clear additional short-term disability and leg-pain benefit
explanation:
The 400-patient trial found minimal or no additional short-term disability or leg-pain benefit from adding glucocorticoid to lidocaine; it had no placebo arm (p1639).

D. A clear additional short-term disability and leg-pain benefit: The reported comparison showed minimal or no short-term benefit (p1639).
C. Proof that steroid injections outperform a placebo injection: The trial included no placebo group (p1639).
A. Proof that lidocaine alone has no effect compared with placebo: Without a placebo arm, that comparison was not made (p1639).

q: מה מהבאים מוגדר כאי ספיקת כליות חדה AKI באישה בת 70 ששוקלת 70 ק"ג?
o: עליה בקראטינין מ- 0.4 ל- 0.8 תוך 24 שעות
קראטינין 0.9 עם אלבומינוריה של 300 mg/g
מתן 400cc שתן ב 6 שעות
עליה באוריאה מ- 50 ל- 80 תוך 3 ימים
keySource: IMA 2026-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q124
explanation:
**Official answer:** A (IMA 2026-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q124).

**Official source:** Harrison · ch. 321 · p. 2372.

A creatinine rise from 0.4 to 0.8 within 24 hours meets AKI criteria even though the final value may lie within the laboratory reference interval (p. 2372).

**A. Creatinine doubles within 24 hours.** Correct, the increase is 0.4 mg/dL and twice baseline, satisfying the source's acute creatinine criteria (p. 2372).
**B. Creatinine 0.9 with albuminuria.** Wrong, albuminuria alone does not establish an acute creatinine rise or low urine output (p. 2372).
**C. 400 mL of urine over six hours.** Wrong, for 70 kg this is about 0.95 mL/kg/hour, above the oliguria threshold of 0.5 mL/kg/hour (p. 2372; calculation from case data).
**D. Urea rises over three days.** Wrong, the diagnostic definition uses creatinine change or urine output; urea change alone is not a criterion (p. 2372).

Source: Harrison 22e, chapter(s) 321, printed pp. 2372.

q: מה מהבאים מהווה את הסיבוך המאוחר ביותר של אוטם שריר הלב?
o: Left Ventricular Aneurysm
Ventricular Tachycardia
Papillary Muscle Rupture
Pericarditis
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 286 – ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q114
explanation:
**Official answer:** A (IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q114).

**Official source:** Harrison · ch. 275, 305 · pp. 2065, 2255.

Left ventricular aneurysm is the accepted late complication. The source places its complications weeks to months after STEMI, contrasting with early electrical and mechanical complications (pp. 2122-2125).

**A. Left ventricular aneurysm.** Correct, a true aneurysm is scar-based, and its complications usually emerge weeks to months after STEMI (p. 2125).
**B. Ventricular tachycardia.** Wrong, ventricular arrhythmias can occur early during acute ischemia; late VT also occurs, so this is not an absolute statement that all VT precedes aneurysm (pp. 2123-2124).
**C. Papillary muscle rupture.** Wrong, the table describes peaks within 24 hours and at 3-5 days, with a 1-14-day range (p. 2122).
**D. Pericarditis.** Wrong, acute epicardial inflammation is described during STEMI; this option is interpreted as early infarct-associated pericarditis, not every delayed post-injury syndrome (p. 2125).

Source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22nd edition, chapter(s) 286, pp. 2122-2125.
